rows.note: Use 可以 as the all-purpose casual choice when something is acceptable or okay, especially in an evaluation.

example.english: This phone is still all right to use.
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 din6 waa2 zung6 ho2 ji5 jung6

rows.note: Use 冇事 to reassure someone that a person is unharmed or that a thing has no problem.

example.english: You’re all right, don’t be scared.
example.jyutping: nei5 mou5 si6 aa3 m4 sai2 geng1

rows.note: Use 唔錯 as the all-purpose way to say that something went or worked reasonably well.

example.english: The movie was all right overall.
example.jyutping: tou3 hei3 gei2 hou2 tai2 zing2 tai2 m4 co3

rows.note: Use 真係 when “all right” emphatically confirms that something really happened or is certainly true.

example.english: Ming really did come first in the exam, all right.
example.jyutping: aa3 ming4 zan1 hai6 haau2 dou3 dai6 jat1 ming4
